newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-COURT ALLOWS DEPORTIVO TO PLAY AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COURT ALLOWS DEPORTIVO TO PLAY AT HOME.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna had the one match closure of their Riazor stadium suspended on Friday after taking their case to a Spanish civil court.
The landmark decision by Madrid's Supreme Tribunal means that Deportivo can now play Barcelona at home on January 4 instead of travelling to a neutral venue.
The ground closure was imposed in October by Spain's Committee for Sporting Discipline after the referee was struck in the face by a coin thrown from the crowd in the match against Rayo Vallecano.

Some Spanish clubs condemned the decision. "This could even paralyse the league," said Sporting Gijon president Jose Fernandez "All of us could appeal in all cases. It could be very serious." he said.
But his Deportivo counterpart Augusto Lendoiro was adamant that going to court was a fundamental democratic right, and those that denied it were living "in another century".
"They say that a club can't go to the law courts, it's unbelievable," said Lendorio.
